The only eviction is Shutdown/drop. README.md:57-61 tells the host to reopen, but OpenNamespace returns the same stale handle. After a post-rename directory-fsync uncertainty the namespace is still attached, so OpenNamespace and ReadSnapshot report the old revision while disk holds the new snapshot; a retry from that state can diverge or overwrite the unacknowledged revision. No poison/evict/reopen path exists. Prior test only injects replacement before the final check and never drives the server reopen path.

(2) Final attachment check is detection, not an atomic path-attachment guarantee. src/component/store/anchored.rs:536-546 runs the final ensure_attached after publish, but then commit assigns self.snapshot, builds CommitOutcome, returns through handle_commit, encodes, writes, and flushes the frame; rollback is identical. A replacement/rename after the check (or after its statat but before the ack) still yields Committed/RolledBack for a detached inode. README.md:78-81 claims replacement is checked "immediately before commit/rollback acknowledgement" and "never a success acknowledgement"; src/fs_at.rs:213-216 similarly claims the caller can avoid acknowledging an orphaned write. Both overclaim: identity is the opened directory inode, the pathname check is best-effort, and a successful response cannot guarantee the inode remains reachable at the namespace path. Tests cover replacement before the final check only. The contract/docs must be corrected; the check should remain a detection/eviction trigger, not a claimed atomic path attachment.

(3) Post-write attachment/recovery errors map to Io, and uncertainty is not typed on the wire. src/component/store/anchored.rs:690-697 maps only Ok(false)/NotFound to Uncertain and every other stat error to Io. Post-write call sites at 673 (after the recovery snapshot publish) and 686 (recover_then_check_attached) therefore return Io after the target may be committed; journal removal at 674 uses map_write_error and returns Io for unlink/other failures after publication. Also src/component/store/anchored.rs:517-523 ignores journal unlink failure on a pre-snapshot failure and returns the original Io/Corrupt while a valid journal remains, so a later recovery applies the unacknowledged target (contradicts src/component/store.rs:20-26 and README.md:85-86); first-commit previous removal at 493-496 is also ignored, leaving revision 1 rollback-able to a stale previous. At the wire boundary src/component/server.rs:342 maps StoreErrorKind::Uncertain to ErrorKind::Io, so even a correct internal classification is indistinguishable from ordinary Io except by matching the message string; there is no distinct wire code or documented error contract (see CodeRabbit thread src/component/server.rs:342).

IoError has no is_uncertain accessor. Docs at src/atomic_io.rs:90-92 and 254-256 still claim a failed commit leaves the previous destination intact, which is false after rename. Generic session/KV callers (Core SessionFileBackend/KvCommitBackend seams) can observe Err while the new bytes are installed and must not treat it as an ordinary safe-to-retry failure.
